## Outcome
Ship a reusable, agent-assisted batch process through the installed ZzzOps CLI for migrating supported open legacy goals to the current schema and reviewed normal workflow, without repository-specific helper scripts, manually assembled artifacts or ad hoc migration-policy setup.

## Acceptance criteria
- The installed public workflow discovers eligible open legacy goals, or accepts an explicit goal selection, and prepares a bounded batch using a shipped trusted migration entry. Detect supported predecessor contracts safely; unsupported or malformed records receive actionable per-goal diagnostics without blocking unrelated compatible work. Leave closed goals archived unless explicitly selected for reopening; targeted historical reads remain allowed.
- Prepare and durably publish the exact immutable source snapshot and current-schema specification, graph, payload and identity envelope through supported CLI contracts. Preserve complete human specifications, acceptance criteria, priority, relationships, blockers and every transaction/history record. Preserve dependency/parent authority and ordering. Carry no stale ownership or fabricated evidence, review or approval into active execution.
- Produce a durable reviewable batch manifest binding membership and every source, target, independent review and remaining evidence obligation to exact immutable identities. Require independent review of each conversion. Support one explicit root-coordinated human approval covering the exact manifest, with individual exclusions or changes requested; changing an approved member invalidates its affected approval before activation.
- Schedule independent members within reviewed concurrency/resource limits and respect relationships and dependencies. Batch operation must not imply one cross-goal atomic transaction or grant workers canonical mutation/integration authority. A member failure or human blocker must not erase successful progress or prevent unrelated approved members from proceeding.
- Activation uses exact reviewed conversion and approval evidence, verifies provider state and returns each member's actual normal-workflow next gate. Migration itself completes no product criteria and grants no implementation authority. Preserve truthful per-member statuses, summaries and blockers; report a batch complete only when all required included members have observed outcomes, with explicit exclusions preserved.
- Persist resumable per-member state and stable retry identities across interruption, uncertain provider responses, partial artifact publication and partial activation. Avoid duplicate issues/artifacts/activation or lost history, and never overwrite concurrent user edits. Lease expiry alone grants no takeover; recovery requires supported stopped-owner evidence.
- Keep repository project policy, model inventory and unrelated instructions intact. Use the existing reviewed migration-policy authority; adoption must have a readable bounded preview and any genuinely required approval, without requiring users to construct a custom five-node graph for each repository.
- Prove bounded public installed-CLI journeys in a clean synthetic repository for a multi-goal batch, independent review and batch approval, related goals, mixed valid/invalid records, unsupported predecessors, closed-goal isolation, per-member rejection/exclusion, concurrent edits, interruption at durable boundaries, retry/resume and verified activation. No manual cache copying, private engine-handler invocation or raw provider rewrite may substitute for the shipped workflow.

## Evidence and first falsifiable probe
The current live migration of #573 required a repository-specific reviewed five-node migration entry, helper scripts to prepare and publish immutable artifact layers, independent review, root approval and activation. The engine supports generic migration contracts, but no existing goal explicitly owns packaging this complete reusable batch workflow. In a clean synthetic repository with reviewed ordinary defaults and multiple legacy goals, invoke the installed public workflow and verify whether it supplies the complete migration-entry and batch preparation/review/approval/resume contracts without helper scripts or ad hoc project policy. Preserve the failing boundary before implementation and use the same journey as the corrected control.

## Relationships and scope
Build on #498's migration engine and #522's migration repairs. #577 owns native v2 creation of new goals; #542 owns uncertain-create idempotency and #434 broader independent batch coordination. Inspect and reuse their actual integrated contracts rather than inventing mandatory dependencies or duplicating their broader outcomes. This goal owns the shipped existing-goal migration orchestration, artifacts and batch user/agent contracts. Do not bulk migrate live repositories merely to implement the feature, reset policy, fabricate compatibility for never-shipped states or bundle unrelated repairs. Preserve #573 then #523 and the previously directed queue; priority alone is not a shortcut.

## Risks and authority
Risks include state/history loss, incorrect dependency ordering, stale approval, duplicate external writes, unsupported compatibility assumptions and false batch completion. Treat this as agentic engineering rigor with external-state risk; root retains human interaction and canonical writes. The user requested a durable goal and prefers batch processing. This capture defines required work; source implementation and live migration follow their applicable workflow authority and reviews. All acceptance work is required; unrelated enhancements belong to separate goals.
